## Prompt templates as a read-only resource

nemotron://prompts lists every template; nemotron://prompts/{id} returns one. The resource is generated from the loaded prompts.yaml (packaged file plus any user override), the same objects the request builder uses, so it cannot drift. prompts\_version changes whenever any text or flag set changes, and results echo it. A unit test asserts that every template id the request builder can produce appears in the resource, and the golden-file tests (M2) run each template against the real model.

```
GET nemotron://prompts { "prompts_version": "2026-10-30.2", "model_card_checked": "2026-10-30", "flag_sets": {"B": {"temperature": 0, "top_p": 1.0, "seed": 0, "max_tokens": 16384, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}, "TS": {"mm_processor_kwargs": {"capture_ctc_timestamps": true}}, "QA": {"temperature": 0.6, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": -1, "max_tokens": 20480, "thinking_token_budget": 17408, "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true, "reasoning_budget": 16384}}}, "templates": [ {"id": "near_field", "tool": "transcribe", "selected_when": "near_speaker_only=true; style unset or raw_dictation", "where_it_fits": "Dictation and voice interfaces with background speakers", "system": null, "user": "Transcribe this audio. Include all spoken words ... Do not transcribe any other voices.", "placeholders": [], "flags": ["B"], "status": "card-verbatim, experimental", "source": "model card, Prompt Guide"}, ... ] }
```

## Resources

- nemotron://limits: the effective limits table as JSON, each value with its source, as last computed by check\_backend
- nemotron://languages and nemotron://languages/{code}: the loaded languages.yaml (41 languages by 7 capabilities)
- nemotron://config: the effective config.yaml with the origin of each value; never the endpoint, API key or model id
- nemotron://prompts: every prompt template from the loaded prompts.yaml with its tool, selection rule, flags, status, origin and version (read-only)
- nemotron://prompts/{id}: one template
- transcripts://{job\_id}: the finished transcript text; transcripts://{job\_id}/words, /srt, /vtt, /md and /meta: the other artifacts, backed by the files in the job folder (section 5a)
- transcripts://batch/{batch\_id}: summary of a playlist or folder batch

# skeleton (mcp v2)

from mcp.server import MCPServer mcp = MCPServer("nemotron-transcribe", instructions="Audio files must live under /data/audio. Chunking is handled for you. If a call fails with backend errors, run check\_backend.")

## Prompts

- meeting\_notes(path): speakers + timestamps, then summarize with the agent's own LLM
- subtitles(path, language): transcribe with word timestamps, fetch srt
- quote\_finder(path, topic): transcribe, then locate by timestamp

```
@mcp.tool() async def check_backend(deep: bool = False, probe_limits: bool = False) -> BackendReport: """Check the configured Nemotron endpoint: reachability, model id, context length, audio limits.""" @mcp.tool() async def transcribe(path: str, style: Literal["verbatim", "clean", "technical", "raw_dictation"] | None = None, # None = auto context_terms: list[str] | None = None, speakers: int | None = None, # 2..8 word_timestamps: bool = False, near_speaker_only: bool = False, # experimental language: str = 'auto', script_hint: str = 'standard', code_switching: bool = False, wait_seconds: int = 25) -> JobResult: """Speech to text ... (the full description text above; this docstring is what the agent reads)""" spec = resolve_transcribe(style, context_terms, speakers, word_timestamps, near_speaker_only, caps=await backend_caps()) # spec.template (id, version), spec.user_text, spec.flags, spec.warnings; raises ToolError(code, message, hint) bundle = load_all() # packaged defaults < user config dir < env vars (section 5c) PROMPTS_VERSION = bundle.prompts.prompts_version # PromptTemplate is the pydantic model in models.py, loaded from prompts.yaml; fields shown for reference @dataclass(frozen=True) class PromptTemplate: id: str; tool: str; system: str | None; user: str # user has {placeholders} flags: tuple[str, ...] # names into FLAG_SETS: B, TS, QA status: str; source: str; where_it_fits: str # all published by nemotron://prompts if __name__ == "__main__": startup_check() # logs the report; exits only when NEMOTRON_STARTUP_CHECK=strict if os.getenv("MCP_TRANSPORT") == "http": mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", host="0.0.0.0", port=8080) else: mcp.run()
```

## 5. Bookkeeping design (ffmpeg core)

ffmpeg and ffprobe live in the MCP image and do every step before and after the model. Commands below were syntax-checked on this box against a synthetic file; silencedetect, slicing and normalization behaved as described. Thresholds are my starting points. Every size, duration and token budget comes from the effective limits of the configured backend (section 3), never from constants.

## Step 1: probe

```
ffprobe -v error -select_streams a:0 \ -show_entries format=duration,size,format_name,bit_rate:stream=codec_name,sample_rate,chann els,channel_layout \ -of json "$IN"
```

Reject when the streams list is empty (no audio) or duration is missing. Record duration, source size and channels, then compute tokens: audio = ceil(12.5 x duration), transcript estimate = 6 x duration. Optional integrity pass: ffmpeg -v error -i IN -f null - (any output means a damaged file). Multi-track video: expose an audio\_stream index and use -map 0:a:N.

## Step 2: normalize to the model's input

```
# 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM WAV: what the model sees [S1]; 115.2 MB per hour ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -y -threads 2 -i "$IN" -vn -map 0:a:0 -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le \ -progress pipe:1 -nostats "$WORK/norm.wav" # smaller archive copy (not sent to the model unless chunking size demands it) ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -y -i "$WORK/norm.wav" -c:a flac -compression_level 8 "$WORK/norm.flac"
```

Normalizing also removes most size problems: 16 kHz mono WAV is 115.2 MB per hour, under the 180 MB the card's server uses, and the decoded float32 size (219.7 MiB) fits under the 180 MB the card's server uses, and the decoded float32 size (219.7 MiB) fits vLLM's 256 MiB decode guard [S7]. It does not fit vLLM's default 25 MB or 600 s, which is why the limits must be configured (step 4 shows the effect). Skip re-encoding only when the source is already 16 kHz mono PCM WAV. Loudness normalization is off by default because no WER evidence supports it; test in evals.

## Step 3: silence map

```
# do not use -v error here: silencedetect logs at info level on stderr ffmpeg -hide_banner -nostats -i "$WORK/norm.wav" \ -af silencedetect=noise=-35dB:d=0.5 -f null - 2>&1 | grep silence_ # silence_start: 4.999937 # silence_end: 7.000125 | silence_duration: 2.000188
```

Parse into (start, end, duration, midpoint). If a long meeting has no usable silence, retry with noise=-30dB:d=0.3, then fall back to a hard cut. The same map flags suspect output: words timed inside a silence of 5 s or more are likely invented text, which the NeMo-Speech.cpp docs warn can happen on noise or music [S9] (design idea, to be validated).

## Step 4: plan chunks from the effective limits

```
@dataclass class Limits: # produced by check_backend; every field also carries a source tag context_tokens: int # queried max_model_len [S14], or NEMOTRON_CONTEXT_TOKENS max_audio_s: float # NEMOTRON_MAX_AUDIO_S / preset / learned max_audio_bytes: int # NEMOTRON_MAX_AUDIO_MB x 1,000,000 (MB vs MiB unverified; the smaller is the safe reading) def budget_max_s(L: Limits, prompt_tokens: int, reasoning: bool) -> float: ctx = L.context_tokens - prompt_tokens - 64 # margin token_s = (ctx - 20480) / 12.5 if reasoning else ctx / (12.5 + 6.0) # [S1][S4][S9] size_s = 0.98 * L.max_audio_bytes / 32000 # 16 kHz mono s16 WAV = 32,000 bytes per second return min(token_s, L.max_audio_s - 5, size_s, 3300) # 3300 s = 55 min, as NVIDIA's long-form eval [S4] def plan(dur, silences, L, prompt_tokens, reasoning, speakers: bool):
```

def plan(dur, silences, L, prompt\_tokens, reasoning, speakers: bool):

```
hard_max = budget_max_s(L, prompt_tokens, reasoning) cuts, start = [], 0.0 while dur - start > hard_max: window = [s for s in silences if start + 0.8*hard_max <= s.mid <= start + hard_max] cut = max(window, key=lambda s: s.dur).mid if window else start + 0.9*hard_max cuts.append((cut, "silence" if window else "hard")) start = cut # overlap: 0 s at a silence cut for plain transcripts; 10 s when speakers matter; # 5 s at a hard cut [S4]
```

| Backend limits                                                  | hard_max (300-token prompt, reasoning off)         | 1 h file becomes                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| context 65,536; 600 s; 25 MB (vLLM defaults)                    | min(3,523, 595, 766, 3,300) = 595 s (9.9 min)      | 7 chunks. Speaker reconciliation gets harder; the startup warning says how to raise the caps      |
| context 65,536; 3,600 s; 180 MB (card preset)                   | min(3,523, 3,595, 5,512, 3,300) = 3,300 s (55 min) | 2 chunks (55 min + 5 min), or 1 chunk if you set the cap to 3,600 s and accept the thinner margin |
| context 32,768 (server started with a smaller --max-model- len) | about 1,750 s (29 min)                             | 3 chunks                                                                                          |

Values in the table are my arithmetic from the formula above (derived). Entity-list budget: tokenize the terms with the checkpoint's tokenizer.json (it is in the repo), dedupe, keep the user's order, cap at about 1,500 tokens (my default), and return a warning naming what was dropped. The cap feeds budget\_max\_s, so a bigger list shortens chunks. Safe maximum list size is not documented: the Contextual Earnings22 'global' setting uses a whole-call keyword inventory but its size is not stated [S4]. Measure WER against list size (0, 50, 200, 1,000 terms) in the evals.

## Step 5: slice

```
ffmpeg -nostdin -v error -y -ss "$START" -to "$END" -i "$WORK/norm.wav" \
```

```
# per chunk, re-encoded: sample-accurate -c:a pcm_s16le "$WORK/chunk_003.wav"
```

Measured on this box: asking for 4.5 s to 9.25 s gave exactly 4.750 s with re-encode, but 4.800 s with -c copy; the segment muxer (-f segment -segment\_times ... -c copy) drifted by up to 48 ms per cut. Use the per-chunk command, then ffprobe each chunk and store its real start offset, so timestamps never accumulate drift. Pipe through stdin for very long files if disk is a concern.

## Step 6: transcribe, stitch, re-offset

1. Send chunks to the endpoint with a small concurrency (max\_concurrent\_requests, default 1, section 5g); vLLM batches. Timestamp requests are one audio each [S1].
2. Re-offset: global\_t = chunk\_start + t for every word; for hard cuts keep words from the left chunk up to the overlap midpoint and from the right chunk after it.
3. Without timestamps, dedupe overlaps by longest common suffix/prefix over about 30 words (fuzzy, rapidfuzz).
4. Run the loop guardrail per chunk, then join. Write transcript.txt, words.json, subtitles.srt/vtt under the job directory.
5. Hard problem: speaker labels. Diarization indices are local to each request [S4]. Plan: avoid chunking when a file fits; otherwise use a 10 s overlap and map labels with the Hungarian algorithm on word co-occurrence in the overlap; report a speaker\_map\_confidence and mark low-confidence chunk boundaries instead of guessing. A silence cut with no overlap cannot be reconciled, hence the overlap for speaker tasks. Needs real multi-speaker test audio to tune.

## Jobs, progress and failure handling

- Queue, persistence, restart and cancellation are specified in section 5a; this list covers states, retries and transport.
- States: queued, downloading (URLs only), probing, normalizing, chunking, transcribing (k of n), stitching, done, failed, cancelled, plus waiting\_for\_backend. Progress is completed audio seconds over total; ETA from observed throughput.
- Progress goes out two ways: progress notifications while a call is waiting, and

get\_job\_status polling. Polling is the primary path; see section 5a [S13][S39].

- get\_job\_status polling. Polling is the primary path; see section 5a [S13][S39].
- Retries: 429 or 5xx with backoff; on a context, size or duration error, re-plan that chunk smaller (halve) and retry once; empty output on speech triggers one retry. Check ctc\_timestamps.error before trusting timestamps [S1].
- Security: resolve paths and require them inside AUDIO\_ROOT; bearer token on the MCP HTTP port; bind to 127.0.0.1 by default; label returned text as untrusted.
- Transport to the endpoint starts as a base64 data URL (documented) [S1]. Later options: an HTTP URL served by the MCP container (vLLM fetch timeout 10 s, download cap 256 MB by default) or file:// with --allowed-local-media-path; the latter is documented for images, audio support unverified [S7][S8].

## Operations and co-tenancy

On your Spark the Nemotron server is not alone: other models share the same 128 GB unified memory pool, and the OS, page cache, ffmpeg and the MCP draw from it too. Because the MCP is a pure client, it cannot control the server's memory, but it can avoid making contention worse and can fail gracefully.

- The memory cap on the server is per instance and does not coordinate with other processes [S17]. Whoever starts last may find less free memory than planned, and a busy co-tenant can push a running server into OOM during a long request. Treat backend connection resets and 5xx during a job as possible OOM, not as bad input.
- The MCP keeps concurrency low (default 1) and sends one chunk per request; a smaller max\_concurrent\_requests or a shorter chunk cap reduces the server's peak activation memory. The encoder activation peak for a 55 to 60 minute request has not been measured by anyone I found, and the NVFP4 card tells operators to validate headroom for long recordings under the intended load [S2].
- On a connection error or 5xx the job moves to waiting\_for\_backend, re-runs check\_backend with exponential backoff, resumes from the last completed chunk, and halves the chunk size and the concurrency on a repeated failure. It never restarts or reconfigures the server.
- check\_backend reports latency and recent failure counts, so an agent (or you) can see whether the endpoint is degrading.
- On the client side: ffmpeg runs with -threads 2, the container has a 2 GB limit, and the MCP reads one chunk at a time (a 55 minute chunk is about 105 MB of WAV, about 140 MB as base64) so it stays small next to the models.

## 5a. Long-running work: jobs, progress, notifications

Transcribing a long file, or a downloaded video, takes minutes, and throughput on your hardware is not measured yet (the card benchmarks use data-center GPUs, section 2). A single blocking tool call cannot be the mechanism: opencode times out MCP requests, tool calls included, after 30 s by default [S28], and Hermes after 300 s per tool call [S29]. The spec tells implementations to set request timeouts, allows resetting them on progress notifications, and requires a maximum timeout regardless [S38].

## What the MCP spec offers, and who can use it

| Mechanism                                       | Spec status (revision 2026-07-28)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Progress notifications (progressToken)          | Core utility. The client puts a progressToken server sends notifications/progress with value, optional total and message, on the that request [S35][S39]. Python SDK v2: ctx.report_progress(progress, total, client sent no token [S39].                                                                                                                                               |
| Tasks extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks) | Official extension; moved out of the core the experimental 2025-11-25 design is [S35][S36]. The server answers tools/call (resultType task); the client polls tasks/get input_required, completed, failed, tasks/update and tasks/cancel server decides per request, and only for the extension. Optional notifications/tasks subscriptions/listen. Progress notifications tasks [S36]. |
| Resource subscriptions and notifications        | resources/subscribe was replaced by long-lived stream where the client opts resourceSubscriptions and other                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Cancellation                                    | notifications/cancelled (stdio) or closing (Streamable HTTP) cancels the in-flight should stop and not reply [S38]. Tasks tasks/cancel [S36].                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

Job-handle tools

## Recommendation: job-handle tools first.

transcribe waits up to wait\_seconds (default 25, below opencode 30 s default timeout [S28]) and sends progress notifications while it waits. If the job is not finished it returns a job\_id plus a ready-made sentence telling the agent what to do next. Tasks and resource subscriptions become extra layers over the same job store when SDK and clients catch up; they never replace the tools. There is no separate start\_job: wait\_seconds=0 is start\_job, which avoids two ways of doing one thing.

## Job tools: portable, work in every client

The tools are in the section 4 table (transcribe and the other model tools, get\_job\_status, get\_job\_result, cancel\_job, list\_jobs). Every response that involves a job uses one shape, so the agent never has to guess:

```
{ "job_id": "j_7Qe3xK9mP2vL5nRt8WcA1g", "state": "running", "stage": "transcribing", "progress": { "done_s": 2160, "total_s": 5400, "chunks_done": 2, "chunks_total": 5 }, "eta_s": 310, "retry_after_s": 30, "cached": false, "source": { "kind": "url", "extractor": "youtube", "id": "VIDEO_ID", "title": "(untrusted text)" }, "message_for_agent": "Still transcribing (40 percent, about 5 minutes left). Tell the user it is running. Call get_job_status with this job_id later or when the user asks; do not poll in a loop.", "result_paths": null // when done: { "txt": "/home/me/.local/share/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/jobs/j_.../transcript.txt", "srt": "...", "json": "..." } }
```

tasks/cancel [S36].

Ordinary tools. For state across calls the 2026servers to use explicit, server-minted handles p tool arguments [S35].

The description of transcribe says that a running job is normal and that the agent should report it to the user instead of waiting silently, because most agents otherwise retry or give up. That wording is part of the tool contract and is tested in M2 with a real agent.

## Persistence, worker and idempotency

```
-- jobs.db in the OS user data dir (WAL mode). Created and migrated on start. CREATE TABLE jobs ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, -- random 128-bit, unguessable idem_key TEXT NOT NULL, -- sha256 of source identity + settings (below) state TEXT NOT NULL, -- queued | running | done | failed | cancelling | cancelled stage TEXT, -- downloading | probing | normalizing | chunking | transcribing | stitching kind TEXT, source_kind TEXT, source TEXT, source_id TEXT, settings_json TEXT, batch_id TEXT, created_at TEXT, started_at TEXT, finished_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, done_s REAL, total_s REAL, error_code TEXT, error_message TEXT, result_dir TEXT ); CREATE INDEX jobs_idem ON jobs(idem_key, state); CREATE TABLE chunks (job_id TEXT, idx INT, start_s REAL, end_s REAL, state TEXT, attempts INT, text_path TEXT, words_path TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (job_id, idx)); CREATE TABLE events (job_id TEXT, ts TEXT, level TEXT, message TEXT);
```

- Worker: one asyncio scheduler task owns the queue and starts up to NEMOTRON\_MAX\_JOBS jobs (default 1). Downloads and ffmpeg preparation of queued jobs may run ahead (up to 2) so the GPU never waits. The only gate in front of the model is one global limit, max\_concurrent\_requests (default 1, section 5g), shared by every job. The shared Spark therefore sees at most that many requests from this tool.
- Restart: a startup sweep puts running jobs back to queued; finished chunks (the chunks table) are reused and an interrupted download resumes from its partial file. With stdio the server exits when the client exits, so an interrupted job resumes the next time any client launches the server, or with jobs resume. For jobs that must finish after you close the client, run serve --http as a user service (doctor prints a

launchd or systemd unit); this is a design proposal for M6.

- launchd or systemd unit); this is a design proposal for M6.
- Idempotency key: sha256 of canonical JSON of the source identity plus the settings. Source identity: a local file is size plus a hash of its first and last MiB (so renames still hit); a URL is the yt-dlp extractor name plus video id (plus the playlist item). Settings: tool, style, speakers, word\_timestamps, near\_speaker\_only, target language, the final merged context\_terms, prompts\_version and the served model id. Not in the key: wait\_seconds, notification options, concurrency. A new prompts\_version or model id invalidates old cache entries on its own.
- Behavior: same key already done returns that job at once with cached true. Same key queued or running returns the same job\_id, so a retrying agent never starts a duplicate. Same key failed or cancelled starts a new job unless the call asked to reuse partial work. force=true bypasses the cache.
- Retention: transcripts and metadata are kept 30 days by default (NEMOTRON\_KEEP\_DAYS, my number); downloaded and normalized audio is deleted when the job ends unless keep\_audio is set; jobs clean removes everything older.
- Security: job ids are random because the Tasks extension requires task ids that cannot be guessed [S36] and the same ids are reused there; result paths are only returned from inside the job folder; transcript and title text is labeled untrusted in every response.

## Tasks extension adapter (later)

- Detect support per request: the client declares extensions io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in its per-request capabilities, and the server advertises it in server/discover [S36]. A server must not return a task handle to a client that did not declare it [S36].
- With the capability: transcribe and the other model tools return a task handle (taskId equal to job\_id, status working, pollIntervalMs 5000, ttlMs equal to retention). tasks/get maps states: queued, running and cancelling become working; done becomes completed with the tool result inline; cancelled becomes cancelled. A tool-level error is completed with isError true, because the spec reserves failed for JSON-RPC errors [S36]. tasks/cancel calls cancel\_job. Status text goes in statusMessage, since progress notifications are not supported on tasks [S36].
- Without it: the job-handle result described above. Both read the same job store, so there is one code path for the work and a thin adapter for the protocol.
- Timing: the Python SDK does not implement the extension yet [S37]. The adapter is a milestone after the SDK ships it (M6), not before: hand-writing handlers for a young extension risks spec drift for little gain while no client uses it.

Anywhere a file path is accepted, an http or https URL that yt-dlp supports (YouTube and the many other sites in its extractor list) is accepted too. Once the audio is on disk, the pipeline is the one in section 5, and everything in sections 4 and 5a applies unchanged: this section only adds the front end.

## Chapters as split points

- info[chapters] holds start\_time, end\_time and title when the video has chapters; many do not [S43]. No chapters means the silence-based plan from section 5.
- If the whole file fits in one request there is no cut at all: chapters only become headings and timestamps in transcript.md.
- Otherwise cut at the latest chapter boundary at or before the effective chunk cap, but not earlier than half the cap (no tiny chunks). Snap the cut to the nearest detected silence within 2 s. With no boundary in that window use the silence cut from section 5; a chapter longer than the cap is silence-split inside. The 2 s and half-cap numbers are mine.
- Why: a chapter boundary is a topic change and usually a pause, so cutting there is less likely to split a sentence than a blind cut, and the transcript can be organized by chapter. Speaker tasks still use the overlap rules from section 5.

## Video metadata and context\_terms

- Always returned in the job result and meta.json and never sent to the model: title, uploader, upload date, duration, webpage URL, chapters, and the first 500 characters of the description, all marked untrusted.
- use\_metadata\_terms=true (default false) sends a short term list built from the title, chapter titles and description: capitalized phrases and tokens with digits or mixed case, minus URLs, hashtags, emails, timestamps and stop words, each at most 60 characters, at most 100 terms (my numbers). Your own context\_terms come first. Whether a long list helps or hurts has not been measured; it joins the terms-list size sweep in M5.
- Raw description text is never put into a prompt. It is written by whoever uploaded the video, and the model follows text instructions, so it is a prompt-injection path. Only short extracted terms go through.
- Default is off because descriptions are noisy (sponsor links, chapter spam) and

wrong terms can mislead the transcript. Turn it on for technical talks where the title wrong terms can mislead the transcript. Turn it on for technical talks where the title carries the vocabulary.

## Playlists

- noplaylist is on by default, so a watch URL that also carries a list parameter means that one video.
- A pure playlist or channel URL does not start anything: probe\_audio lists the entries with extract\_flat (titles and ids; durations may be missing in flat mode) and the count, and transcribe returns playlist\_needs\_confirmation with the count and the total duration when known.
- playlist=all or first\_n=N creates a batch: one job per item with a shared batch\_id, all through the same queue, capped by NEMOTRON\_MAX\_PLAYLIST\_ITEMS (default 25, my number). list\_jobs filters by batch\_id and transcripts://batch/{batch\_id} summarizes.
- One private or deleted item does not stop the rest: yt-dlp continues past download errors in a playlist by default [S43], and failed items are listed in the summary. The idempotency key makes a re-run skip finished items.
- The folder batch from the lecture-style workflow uses this same batch machinery with a folder as the source.

## Errors: age-gated, private, geo-blocked and the rest

| Condition       | What yt-dlp reports (community- reported wording; it can change)   | Error code     | What the user is told                                                                                                                                                               |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Age- restricted | Sign in to confirm your age                                        | age_restricted | This video needs a signed-in session. Opt-in only: NEMOTRON_YTDLP _COOKIES_FROM_ BROWSER=firefox uses cookies from your browser (never logged or copied). Consider the account risk |

the account risk

|                          |                                                     |                                       | and the site terms.                                                                                                               |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Private                  | Private video                                       | private_video                         | Only the uploader can grant access. Nothing to retry.                                                                             |
| Geo-blocked              | not available in your country                       | geo_blocked                           | Region-restricted. The tool does not try to bypass this.                                                                          |
| Bot check                | Sign in to confirm you are not a bot                | bot_check                             | Update yt-dlp first (doctor shows its age), retry later, avoid VPN and data-center networks; browser cookies are the last resort. |
| Live or upcoming         | live status in metadata                             | live_not_supported                    | Try again after the stream has ended.                                                                                             |
| Members- only, paid, DRM | various                                             | not_available                         | Not supported.                                                                                                                    |
| Extractor broken         | ExtractorError or HTTP 403 on a normal public video | extractor_outdated                    | Update yt-dlp. The message includes its version and the exact upgrade command.                                                    |
| Network                  | retries exhausted                                   | network_error                         | Job kept and resumable; try again.                                                                                                |
| Too long, or a playlist  | n/a                                                 | too_long, playlist_needs_confirmation | Shows the limit or the entry count and how to continue.                                                                           |

The strings in the second column come from community write-ups, not from a yt-dlp specification (search results, Oct 30, 2026). The mapping therefore matches yt-dlp exception types first and message substrings second, and anything unknown becomes exception types first and message substrings second, and anything unknown becomes ytdlp\_error with the raw message (cleaned and capped at 300 characters). Fixtures for these cases are recorded once, so tests never hit YouTube.

## Keeping yt-dlp working

- Dependency: yt-dlp[default,deno]. PyPI metadata for yt-dlp 2026.10.26 (uploaded Oct 26, 2026) shows a default extra (including yt-dlp-ejs) and a deno extra that pulls the deno package [S43]. YouTube needs a JavaScript runtime for full support (Deno 2.3 or newer is recommended; Node 22, QuickJS and Bun also work) [S42]. The deno PyPI package has wheels for macOS (Intel and arm64), Linux (x86\_64 and aarch64) and Windows x64, so users install nothing extra, including on the Spark.
- YouTube breaks old versions, and the version number is a date. doctor warns when the installed yt-dlp is more than 45 days old (my number). Every extractor\_outdated message includes the version and the command: uv tool upgrade nemotrontranscribe-mcp for a persistent install, or uvx --refresh nemotron-transcribe-mcp doctor for a cached uvx environment (the --refresh flag is from memory; verify).
- Release process: a weekly CI job bumps the yt-dlp lower bound, runs the fixture tests and publishes a patch release, so a plain upgrade is enough for users.
- External binary: NEMOTRON\_YTDLP\_BIN points at a yt-dlp you manage yourself (brew, or the official standalone binary, which updates itself with yt-dlp -U [S43]); metadata then comes from yt-dlp --dump-single-json --skip-download. Useful when YouTube changes faster than our release.
- ffmpeg: this path downloads one audio stream and does no merge or -x conversion, so yt-dlp should not need ffmpeg here (not verified on every site; HLS-only sites may), and we pass our resolved ffmpeg path anyway.

YouTube Terms of Service (version dated Dec 15, 2023) do not allow accessing, downloading or otherwise using content except as expressly authorized by the service or with written permission from YouTube and the rights holders, allow viewing and listening for personal, non-commercial use, and prohibit circumventing features that restrict copying or use of content [S44]. Other sites have their own terms, and a recording can be copyrighted or private. Use this feature only for audio you have the right to process, such as your own uploads, openly licensed material, or content you have permission to use. You are responsible for following the terms of every site you point it at and the law

where you live. This is a design note, not legal advice. Design consequences:

where you live. This is a design note, not legal advice. Design consequences: URL input prints this notice at init and in the README, cookie use is off by default, there is no attempt to bypass geo-blocks, age gates or DRM, and downloaded audio is deleted after the job unless you keep it.

## 5c. Settings as YAML files (languages.yaml, prompts.yaml, config.yaml)

- Design principle: when appropriate, use YAML files for settings the MCP consumes that may need human intervention.

Prompt wording, language support, chunk sizes, server-limit presets, retention and URL caps all live in shipped, commented YAML files that a person can read, diff and override, not in code and not in a long list of environment variables. The endpoint, the API key and the served model id stay in environment variables (Configuration and setup), because they are machine-specific or secret. Facts the code depends on (16 kHz mono, 12.5 audio tokens per second, the speaker and rich-transcription tag syntax) stay in code with a test, because editing them can only break the server.

| File                       | Holds                                                                                                                                           |
|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| languages.yaml             | 41 languages by 7 capabilities, quality tiers, the card FLEURS CoVoST2 numbers, the two language-ID label sets, native and aliases (section 5d) |
| prompts.yaml               | 20 prompt templates (T1 to T16, X1, L1 to L3, Q1), 3 request sets (B, TS, QA) and the word-timestamp modifier                                   |
| config.yaml                | Server-limit presets, chunking, jobs and retention, URL caps, language policy, subtitle line lengths                                            |
| Not YAML: environment only | NEMOTRON_BASE_URL (the endpoint), NEMOTRON_API_KEY, NEMOTRON_MODEL                                                                              |

## Loading order and overrides

1. Packaged defaults: the three files ship as package data and are read with

1. Packaged defaults: the three files ship as package data and are read with

importlib.resources, so they work from a wheel, from uvx and from an .mcpb bundle.

2. User override, per file name: the path in NEMOTRON\_CONFIG\_FILE, NEMOTRON\_LANGUAGES\_FILE or NEMOTRON\_PROMPTS\_FILE if set (a missing file is an error, not ignored), otherwise the file of the same name in the user config dir. The dir is NEMOTRON\_CONFIG\_DIR, else $XDG\_CONFIG\_HOME/nemotrontranscribe-mcp, else ~/.config/nemotron-transcribe-mcp. Using platformdirs for the macOS and Windows locations is my proposal and is not checked.
3. Individual environment variables for single config.yaml values (table below). They win over every file, so a one-off change never needs a file edit.

Merge rules: config.yaml is deep-merged (mappings merge; lists and scalars replace). languages.yaml and prompts.yaml merge by id: an override entry replaces only the keys it names, an unknown id is appended, and replace: true at the top of the file replaces the packaged file entirely. A new model revision therefore needs a user languages.yaml with only the rows that changed. The merged result is validated as a whole, and each layer is recorded, so nemotron://config and doctor can show which file each value came from.

## Validation with friendly errors

All three files are parsed with Pydantic v2 models that forbid unknown keys. A bad file stops the server at startup with a message that names the file, the dotted key path and the offending value, and says how to recover. It does not silently fall back to the default, because a typo in a prompt or a limit should be noticed. These are the real messages from the tests on the box:

```
~/.config/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/config.yaml has 2 problem(s): - jobs.max_jobs: Input should be greater than or equal to 1 (got 0) - jobs.keep_days: Input should be greater than or equal to 0 (got -1) Fix the file, or delete it to fall back to the packaged default. ~/.config/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/config.yaml has 1 problem(s): - limits: limits.preset 'nope' is not defined; choose one of ['nvidiacard', 'vllm-defaults'] Fix the file, or delete it to fall back to the packaged default. ~/.config/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/config.yaml has 1 problem(s): - jobs.base_url: Extra inputs are not permitted (got 'http://x') The endpoint, API key and model id are set with environment variables (NEMOTRON_BASE_URL, NEMOTRON_API_KEY, NEMOTRON_MODEL), never in YAML. Fix the file, or delete it to fall back to the packaged default. ~/.config/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/prompts.yaml has 1 problem(s): - templates.0: verbatim: placeholders used in text ['oops'] differ from declared [] Fix the file, or delete it to fall back to the packaged default.
```

## prompts.yaml: the prompt table as data

The prompt table in section 4 is a rendered snapshot of this file. Every template has an The prompt table in section 4 is a rendered snapshot of this file. Every template has an id, a card reference, the tool that uses it, the task, the exact system and user text with named placeholders, the request flag sets it uses, whether word timestamps are optional, recommended or never, a languages rule that points into languages.yaml (which capabilities must be supported, for which languages), a status and the card section it came from. Status card\_verbatim means the text is exactly the card text. card\_verbatim\_my\_mapping means the text is the card text but choosing it for a tool option is my design. derived means built from a card string by a rule the card does not show (T6). proposal means not on the card; none are used at the moment. A user can fix a wording or add a template by overriding one id in a user prompts.yaml; the result echoes prompts\_version and whether a template came from an override.

```
# prompts.yaml (excerpt of the packaged file) schema_version: 1 prompts_version: '2026-10-30.2' source: {model_id: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B, revision: c17667641642c4265ff2b7037dd101b7d4567634, retrieved: '2026-10-30'} requires_languages_schema_version: 1 flag_sets: B: {description: Base flags for transcription translation and language ID, request: {temperature: 0, top_p: 1.0, seed: 0, max_tokens: 16384, chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}}} TS: {description: Word timestamps (needs the CTC middleware; one audio per request), request: {mm_processor_kwargs: {capture_ctc_timestamps: true}, stream: false, n: 1}} templates: - id: verbatim ref: T1 tool: transcribe task: transcription selected_when: transcribe(path), or style=verbatim user: 'Audio transcription. Language: as spoken. Wording: verbatim, including fillers and repetitions. Formatting: punctuation and capitalization. Output: transcript only.' placeholders: [] flags: [B] word_timestamps: optional languages: {capabilities: [transcription], accept_status: [supported], warn_status: [evaluated_only]} status: card_verbatim - id: translation ref: X1 tool: translate

- T9 (word timestamps) is the modifier word\_timestamps in the file, not a template: it adds flag set TS to any compatible template.
- T11 to T16 are the card benchmark prompts for FLEURS ASR, the three codeswitching sets (ASCEND Mandarin-English, MUCS 2021 Bengali-English and HindiEnglish) and the two Monsoon script instructions. They are reached through the new transcribe options script\_hint (standard, latin, native) and code\_switching; only those pairs have a dedicated prompt, and other languages use T1. Whether T11 beats T1 outside the benchmark is untested.
- L2 and L3 are the wording behind the card language-ID accuracy numbers (FLEURS locale labels, VoxLingua107 codes), so identify\_language uses L2 by default and L1 only for a caller-supplied label list. The label lists are placeholders filled from languages.yaml (lid\_label\_sets), not copied into each template.
- tools/verify\_prompts.py matched all 20 templates against two card revisions (the current main and c421d6a) with 0 differences.

A preset is a name, so someone running a stock vLLM server types nothing and someone using the NVIDIA serve command sets NEMOTRON\_LIMITS\_PRESET=nvidiacard instead of remembering three numbers. When check\_backend probes the real limits, it reports the measured value next to the preset so a wrong preset is visible.

## Resources read from the loaded files

- nemotron://prompts and nemotron://prompts/{id}: the loaded and validated prompts.yaml (packaged plus any override), read-only, with each template origin (packaged or the override path) and prompts\_version. The request builder uses the same objects, so the resource cannot drift from what is sent.
- nemotron://languages and nemotron://languages/{code}: the loaded languages.yaml (section 5d).
- nemotron://config: the effective config.yaml with the origin of each value (packaged, a file path or an env var name). It never includes the endpoint, the API

key or the model id.

- key or the model id.
- Editing a YAML file takes effect on the next server start. Hot reload is not planned: one model revision and one process do not need it.

## CI: validating every YAML file

tests/test\_data\_files.py is the CI test. It passes 21 tests on the box (18 without the card file, 3 more when NEMOTRON\_CARD\_PATH points at a saved copy of the card). It checks that:

- all three packaged files load and validate, their schema\_version and model revision agree, and every user-override case (merge by id, replace, env beats file) behaves as documented;
- languages.yaml has the expected counts (40 transcription, 13 speaker attribution, 31 translation), unique ids and aliases, all 7 capabilities on every row, and the languageID label sets match the per-language labels;
- every prompt references a known flag set and known languages, every placeholder used is declared, and the L2 and L3 label placeholders point at languages.yaml;
- the friendly-error cases produce the messages above (negative value, unknown preset, base\_url in YAML, invalid YAML, a bad prompt override naming its template);
- text is UTF-8 and NFC-normalized, and the resolver finds languages by code, name and alias;
- with the card file: tools/diff\_languages.py reports no drift, tools/verify\_prompts.py reports no problems, and a deliberately changed prompt string is caught.

```
pytest -q # 18 pass, 3 skip without the card NEMOTRON_CARD_PATH=card.md pytest -q # 21 pass python tools/diff_languages.py # live card; exit 0 identical, 1 drift, 2 unreadable python tools/verify_prompts.py prompts.yaml card.md languages.yaml # exit 1 on any mismatch
```

A scheduled weekly CI job runs tools/diff\_languages.py against the live card (the raw README of the model page) and fails on drift, so a model update that changes the language matrix or a prompt is noticed instead of discovered by a user. Both tools use

one shared card parser, so they cannot disagree with each other.

## 5d. Language support (languages.yaml)

Non-English audio is a first-class case, so what the model supports in each language is data, not folklore in tool descriptions. languages.yaml holds the model card language matrix (a row per language, 41 rows) exactly as the card states it, plus the card perlanguage evaluation numbers, and marks anything the card does not say as unknown. It was extracted from the card at revision c176676 (Oct 29, 2026 7:04 PM EDT) and retrieved Oct 30, 2026. The card says 40 languages; the matrix has a 41st row, Norwegian, with a dash in every column, and it is not in the card front-matter list. The matrix tick means Supported and a dash means Not specified, which is not the same as unsupported.

| Capability               | Supported                                   | Other states                                                                                                                                  | Notes                                                                                          |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Transcription            | 40                                          | 1 evaluated only (Norwegian: dash in the matrix, but the FLEURS table has WER 63.76)                                                          | Tiers across the 41 rows: 13 Leading, 15 Production-ready, 13 Supported (may need fine-tuning) |
| Code- switching          | 40                                          | 1 not specified (Norwegian)                                                                                                                   | Own matrix column                                                                              |
| Speaker attribution      | 13 (en fr de hi it ko pt ru es ja th ar zh) | 28 not specified                                                                                                                              | Maximum 8 speakers per request                                                                 |
| Translation to English   | 31                                          | 1 not applicable (English), 5 evaluated only (tr id no tl vi: dash in the matrix, but the card reports scores), 4 not specified (bn mr ta te) | The matrix has one column, Translation <-> English, so both directions share one status        |
| Translation from English | 31                                          | same as above                                                                                                                                 | Same column; the matrix shows 32 ticks because English itself is ticked                        |

| Language ID   | 36 evaluated (FLEURS locale labels; 24 also on VoxLingua107)   | 5 unknown (bn mr no ta te are in neither table)   | Not a matrix column; derived from the card language-ID tables                             |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Audio Q&A     | 1 evaluated (English)                                          | 40 not evaluated                                  | The card says audio Q&A, reasoning and spoken instructions were evaluated in English only |

## Schema

Top level: schema\_version, source (model id, the 40-character revision, its date, card URL, retrieval date, which generator produced the file), curated\_note, the matrix legend and status vocabulary, model-level facts quoted from the card, the two label sets used by language ID, and languages. Each language has the card facts and, in a separate curated block, the few things the card does not give (native name, ISO 639-3, script, direction, aliases). Capability status is one of supported, evaluated\_only, not\_specified, not\_applicable, evaluated, not\_evaluated or unknown, and each capability also records what the matrix showed (check, dash or no\_column) so the file can be diffed against the card mechanically.

```

## Pydantic model and the language parameter

```
# models.py (excerpt): strict models, validated once at startup class Strict(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') class Capability(Strict): status: Literal['supported', 'evaluated_only', 'not_specified', 'not_applicable', 'evaluated', 'not_evaluated', 'unknown'] matrix: Literal['check', 'dash', 'no_column']
```

matrix: Literal['check', 'dash', 'no\_column']

```
note: str | None = None class Language(Strict): id: str = Field(pattern=r'^[a-z]{2,3}$') name_en: str quality_level: Literal['leading', 'production_ready', 'supported'] capabilities: dict[str, Capability] # validator: exactly the 7 known capabilities evaluation: dict lid_labels: dict[str, str | None] curated: Curated # name_native, iso639_3, script, rtl, aliases # LanguagesFile also checks: unique ids and aliases, label sets consistent with per-language labels. # languages.py: LanguageIndex.resolve(text), check_transcribe(...), check_translate(...), check_audio_qa(...), # table(capability), tool_blurb() -> each check returns Verdict(ok, warnings, error, needs_language_id)
```

- The language parameter accepts a code (fr, fr-CA, fra), an English name (French), a native name (Français) or an alias, case-insensitive. Matching uses NFC plus casefold, treats underscore and space as hyphen, falls back from a regional tag to its primary language (en-GB to en), and accepts the FLEURS locale labels (fr\_fr) as aliases. Unknown input returns unknown\_language with the closest matches and a pointer to list\_languages. The aliases are curated by me and are not from the card.
- The default is auto. Plain transcription never needs the language: every transcription prompt says Language: as spoken, so the model finds it on its own. The language matters for the checks and for choosing T11 to T16.
- Tool descriptions and parameter enums are generated from the loaded file (tool\_blurb and the supported-code list), so a user override with a new language shows up in the next start with no code change.

## Capability checks before every request

| Situation                                                       | Result              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| language not in languages.yaml                                  | Error (config       |
| transcribe in a language with status evaluated_only (Norwegian) | Runs with a warning |

| speakers=N in a language without speaker attribution                                                                   | Error                                         |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|

Every error has the same shape as the other tool errors in section 4: code, message, hint and, where there is one, a fallback with the arguments to retry. Every successful result adds a languages block (the resolved language, how it was resolved, the card tier and the warnings), so a calling agent can tell the user what was checked.

## list\_languages and nemotron://languages

- list\_languages(capability optional, supported\_only default true): returns code, English name, native name, tier and, for each capability, its status. With a capability it returns only the languages that have it, for example list\_languages(capability=speaker\_attribution) gives the 13. It reads the same loaded file as the resource, so the two cannot disagree.
- nemotron://languages returns the whole loaded file as JSON; nemotron://languages/{code} returns one language with its evaluation numbers.
- A user override file (NEMOTRON\_LANGUAGES\_FILE or languages.yaml in the user config dir) merges by id, so a new model revision, a new language or a corrected alias needs only the changed rows.
- tools/diff\_languages.py [--card PATH\_OR\_URL] compares the matrix flags, tiers, FLEURS speech-recognition numbers, label sets and the front-matter code list of the file against the card and exits 0 (identical), 1 (drift) or 2 (unreadable). On the box it reports no drift against the live card and against the earlier c421d6a copy.

| FLEURS (google/fleurs) [S52] | Speech recognition and language ID in es, de, fr (Leading), hi, ja and zh (CER for ja and zh), ar, tr and el: the test split of each, compared with the FLEURS column stored in languages.yaml | Hugging Face dataset, CC-BY; 102 languages; about 350 test sentences per language                                                                      | The card lists FLEURS among the training source families and does not say whether test splits were excluded. Treat results as a regression check against the card numbers, not as proof of generalization. |

| out clips                                                           | minutes in the languages Adrian actually uses, with his own reference transcripts   | machine              | certainly not in training   |

Metrics: WER with jiwer, CER where the card uses CER (ko, ja, th, zh, vi); report raw and normalized scores. The card warns that multilingual leaderboard scores use different normalization of accents and compound words and are not directly comparable with the standalone FLEURS numbers, so I compare against the standalone FLEURS column only. Language ID accuracy is measured with L2 on the same clips. The harness reads the measure (WER or CER) and the card baseline from languages.yaml, so adding a language adds a test case.

## 5e. Internationalization

| Concern               | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Basis                                                                                                                      |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Encoding              | UTF-8 everywhere: YAML read as UTF-8, JSON written with ensure_ascii=False, SRT, VTT, markdown and text artifacts written as UTF-8 without a BOM, subprocess arguments passed as lists (never through a shell) so non-ASCII file names and titles survive. Downloaded titles keep their Unicode characters in file names; only characters unsafe in a path are replaced. | WebVTT files are UTF-8 [S54]. SRT has no formal spec, so UTF-8 without BOM is my safe choice (unverified in every player). |
| Unicode normalization | context_terms are normalized                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Unicode FAQ: NFC is the best                                                                                               |

to NFC before they are form for general text; NFKC is Output left untouched No digit or punctuation Design choice The numbers in the subtitles block of config.yaml are Netflix house-style limits that I borrowed as defaults. They are not NVIDIA values and not a standard for every platform, which is why they are in a YAML file a user can change.

|                        | to NFC before they are counted, de-duplicated (casefold) and put into prompt T5. NFKC is not used, because it changes characters such as full-width forms and ligatures. Transcript text is also NFC- normalized on the way out.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | form for general text; NFKC is for identifiers [S55].                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Right-to-left (ar, he) | In WebVTT the base direction of each cue line comes from its first strong character, so a line that starts with a number, punctuation or a Latin name needs an LRM or RLM escape; the writer adds &rlm; at the start of each RTL cue line when bidi_marks is true. In SRT the same effect uses a literal U+200F, which the format does not define. In markdown the speaker label and text are written in logical order; an HTML export gets dir=rtl on RTL paragraphs. | WebVTT spec describes the &lrm; and &rlm; escapes and first-strong-character direction [S54]. The SRT and HTML behavior is unverified; golden fixtures with mixed Arabic and Latin text are part of M2.                                                                                                         |
| CJK line length        | Line length is measured in display columns (full-width CJK character = 2, Latin = 1), not in characters. Packaged defaults: 42 for most languages, ja 26, ko 32, zh 32, ar 42, max 2 lines. Chinese, Japanese and Thai have no spaces, so breaks go at character boundaries (Thai: at word boundaries when a segmenter is available, otherwise at word timestamps); a break never leaves a closing punctuation mark at the start of a line (my rule).                  | Netflix: Japanese 13 full-width characters per line, half-width counts 0.5 [S48]; Korean 16, Latin counts 0.5 [S49]; Simplified Chinese 16 [S50]; most other languages about 42, with Korean and Chinese 16 and Arabic 42 on Originals [S51]. The columns are the same numbers doubled; the conversion is mine. |

| Output left untouched                     | No digit or punctuation localization and no script conversion: full-width punctuation from the model stays. Normalization is applied only inside the eval harness.            | Design choice       |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| Token budget for non- Latin context_terms | Count context_terms conservatively (1 token per character for non-Latin scripts) until the server tokenizer is queried; the cap is config chunking.context_terms_max_ tokens. | My rule, unverified |

## 5f. Observability and logging

Logging decision: the standard library logging module plus a small JSON formatter (about 60 lines, logsetup.py in the prototype), not structlog. Reasons: no extra dependency in a package meant to be started with uvx; libraries that log through the standard library (httpx for example) land in the same JSON stream with no adapter; and contextvars supply job\_id, chunk\_id and stage to every line, so call sites never pass them [S57]. structlog can wrap the standard library and has nicer bound loggers [S60]; it becomes worth its dependency only if the log shape grows beyond what this table shows. One handler set serves both: stderr and a RotatingFileHandler [S58] in the platformdirs user log directory [S59].

## stdout is for MCP messages only.

Over the stdio transport the server must not write anything to stdout that is not a valid MCP message, and may write any logging to stderr [S56]. The logger therefore attaches only stderr and file handlers, never prints, and a test runs a whole simulated job in a child process and asserts that stdout is empty and every stderr line is JSON. A log file that cannot be opened is reported on stderr

## Settings (config.yaml, logging group)

```
jobs: max_cpu_workers: 2 # see 5g logging: level: INFO # env NEMOTRON_LOG_LEVEL: DEBUG | INFO | WARNING | ERROR format: json # json | text; text is for a terminal and only changes stderr, the file is always JSON stderr: true file: enabled: true path: null # env NEMOTRON_LOG_FILE; null = nemotrontranscribe-mcp.log in the user log dir max_bytes: 5242880 # rotate at 5 MiB backup_count: 5 log_transcript_text: false # env NEMOTRON_LOG_TRANSCRIPTS transcript_text_max_chars: 200 mcp_notifications: # deprecated protocol feature (below): off by default enabled: false # env NEMOTRON_LOG_MCP_NOTIFICATIONS level: WARNING status: my_default
```

The default file path comes from platformdirs.user\_log\_dir, which on this Linux box resolves to ~/.local/state/nemotron-transcribe-mcp/log (checked with platformdirs 4.14.0); macOS and Windows locations come from the same call and are unverified here [S59]. The schema is a strict pydantic model like the other groups, so a typo gets the friendly error, and a config that turns off both stderr and the file is rejected because nothing would be logged. The packaged config.yaml, models.py and loader.py in the prototype already contain these keys.

## Line format

| Field   | Present    | Meaning                                                |
|---------|------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| ts      | every line | UTC time with milliseconds and a Z suffix. The summary |

|                                                                        |                          | command converts to your local zone.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| level                                                                  | every line               | DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| logger, event                                                          | every line               | Logger name and a short event name (stage_done, request_retry, job_failed). The event is the stable key; wording of messages can change.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| job_id                                                                 | every line               | null outside a job (startup, doctor)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| stage                                                                  | every line               | download, probe, normalize, slice, request, stitch or total; null when no stage is running                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| chunk_id                                                               | when relevant            | c0, c1, ... for per-chunk work; absent on job-level lines                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| duration_ms                                                            | stage_done, stage_failed | Wall time of the stage, measured with a monotonic clock                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| audio_s, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, attempt, wait_ms, in_flight | request lines            | Audio seconds sent, token counts copied from the usage object of the response, retry attempt number, time spent waiting for the global request slot (5g), and requests in flight when this one finished. Whether the endpoint fills usage for audio requests is unverified: absent counts are logged as null and the summary says so. |
| code, message, hint                                                    | warnings and errors      | The documented error code, what happened, and the next step to take (for example run check_backend, then resume_job)                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

```
{"ts": "2026-10-30T23:41:12.031Z", "level": "INFO", "logger": "nemotron.job", "event": "stage_done", "job_id": "job_f", "stage": "request", "chunk_id": "c0", "duration_ms": 31.0, "attempt": 1, "wait_ms": 0.0, "audio_s": 600.0, "prompt_tokens": 88, "completion_tokens": 2295, "in_flight": 2} {"ts": "2026-10-30T23:41:12.073Z", "level": "WARNING", "logger": "nemotron.job", "event": "request_retry", "job_id": "job_f", "stage": "request", "chunk_id": "c2", "attempt": 1, "http_status": 503, "backoff_s": 0.0, "code": "endpoint_overloaded"} {"ts": "2026-10-30T23:41:12.073Z", "level": "ERROR", "logger": "nemotron.job", "event": "job_failed", "job_id": "job_f", "stage": "total", "chunk_id": "c2", "code": "endpoint_unavailable", "message": "endpoint returned HTTP 503 after 3 attempts", "hint": "Run check_backend, then resume_job; finished chunks are kept."}
```

These three lines come from the prototype running a simulated job (sleeps stand in for ffmpeg and the model, so the timings and token counts mean nothing). They show the format, not performance.

## What is timed and logged

| Stage              | Closing line carries                                  | Other lines in the same stage                                                                                               |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| download           | duration_ms, bytes, host (no path or query string)    | Retries and yt-dlp errors with the section 5b error code and hint                                                           |
| probe (ffprobe)    | duration_ms, duration_s, codec, sample_rate, channels | WARNING limit_warning when the file exceeds an effective limit and gets chunked: limit, value, source (preset or user file) |
| normalize (ffmpeg) | duration_ms per chunk, with chunk_id                  | ffmpeg exit status and the last stderr lines on failure                                                                     |
| slice              | duration_ms per chunk, cut points from silencedetect  | WARNING when no silence is found and a hard cut is used                                                                     |
| request            | duration_ms (latency), wait_ms, audio_s,              | request_retry (attempt, http_status, backoff_s, code)                                                                       |

prompt\_tokens, and WARNING

prompt\_tokens, and WARNING

|        | completion_tokens, attempt, in_flight   | language_fallback (code, language, what was used instead) from the capability checks in section 5d   |
|--------|-----------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| stitch | duration_ms, chunks, speaker_remaps     | WARNING when overlap text could not be matched                                                       |
| total  | duration_ms of the whole job            | job_started, job_done, job_failed, job_cancelled                                                     |

Errors are logged once at the point of failure with the stage, the chunk and a hint a person can act on, and the stage context manager records the failure and re-raises, so the closing lines of enclosing stages show the same cause while unwinding. DEBUG adds the ffmpeg and ffprobe command lines (argument lists, with URL query strings removed) and request sizes.

## Redaction and privacy

| Rule            | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| API keys        | The value of NEMOTRON_API_KEY is registered as an exact-match secret and replaced with <redacted> in every serialized line, including exception text. Regexes also catch Bearer tokens and authorization, api_key, token, password and secret assignments. The key is never a log field in the first place; redaction is the backstop. |
| URLs            | user:password@ is stripped from http and https URLs and query strings are replaced with <redacted>, because signed URLs carry tokens. The host is logged, the full URL is not.                                                                                                                                                         |
| Transcript text | Not logged by default. Fields named text,                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
